You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

First rotate G by 180° to get A. Form the top vertical band as [A | horizontal_flip(A)]; the middle band is [vertical_flip(A) | horizontal_flip(vertical_flip(A))]; the bottom band repeats the top band. Equivalently: each band is the corresponding vertically oriented copy of A, followed horizontally by its left-right reflection. The vertical bands are A, vertical_flip(A), A. Preserve all colors. Important order: each horizontal band starts with the selected A-orientation, then its horizontal reflection (do not reverse this order). Confirmed on three demonstrations: input 8×7→24×14, 1×10→3×20, and 6×14→18×28; also solved a 4×2→12×4 test correctly with no wrong submissions. For the input-row view, output rows are source rows bottom-to-top, top-to-bottom, bottom-to-top; each output row is reverse(source_row) concatenated with source_row. This equivalent row-wise description is useful for direct construction.'), ('arc_expand_grid_with_mirrored_rows_and_horizontal_reflection', 'ARC expand grid with mirrored rows and horizontal reflection', 'For this ARC transformation, an H×W input becomes a (3H)×(2W) output. Build each output row from one input row as reverse(input_row) concatenated with input_row. Select source rows in three blocks: input rows bottom-to-top, then top-to-bottom, then bottom-to-top. Equivalently source indices: H−1…0, 0…H−1, H−1…0. Examples: for input rows [a,b,c], outputs use c,b,a,a,b,c,c,b,a; each row is reversed(row)|row. For H=1, the three output rows are identical, each reverse(the sole row)|the sole row. Demonstrated on 2×5→6×10, 3×5→9×10, and task-620c4650 (9×6 demo to 27×12; 10×6 test to 30×12, submitted correctly). Preserve cell colors exactly.')]
